title: Notifications and Bulk Data Exchange knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly listed as a subtopic of “Notifications and Bulk Data Exchange”?
options: An unrelated requirement that is not named in this lesson
A production change that skips validation
A feature from a different database technology
questions.explanation: The attached PostgreSQL curriculum lists “LISTEN and NOTIFY” beneath “Notifications and Bulk Data Exchange”. Keep the lesson anchored to those listed topics before adding extra material.

questions.prompt: Which workflow best supports a correct implementation of notifications and bulk data exchange?
options: Assume one successful example proves security and recovery
Apply the largest possible change before collecting a baseline
Define the expected behavior and prerequisites, make the smallest change in an isolated environment, then verify both success and an important edge case.
Concatenate user input into SQL and remove permission checks
questions.answer_key: Define the expected behavior and prerequisites, make the smallest change in an isolated environment, then verify both success and an important edge case.
questions.explanation: A controlled example makes the prerequisites and expected behavior explicit. Verification of an edge case helps show whether the idea behind notifications and bulk data exchange is understood.

questions.prompt: When an example related to notifications and bulk data exchange produces an unexpected result, what is the strongest next step?
options: Ignore the returned result and assume the write succeeded
Capture the exact error and context, inspect relevant state or logs, test one hypothesis at a time, and document the verified result.
Disable constraints and retry until the command succeeds
Grant administrator privileges to every application role
questions.answer_key: Capture the exact error and context, inspect relevant state or logs, test one hypothesis at a time, and document the verified result.
questions.explanation: Database troubleshooting should be evidence-led and performed with suitable permissions. Broad privileges or disabling integrity checks may hide the cause and create new failures.
